# NPM Improved v1.7.0 — Security and Recovery Hardening

**Security release.** This release includes the runtime fixes from v1.6.15 plus further hardening of the native host updater, release publication process, and management API.

## Security hardening
- Rejected mismatched image/version requests and invalid rollback targets in the privileged native host dispatcher.
- Bounded queue-file reads and required regular files when accepting update requests.
- Rejected world-writable native updater data directories.
- Prevented forced native host-updater downgrades.
- Rejected duplicate or excessively expanded entries in downloaded updater archives.
- Hardened staging paths and validated compressed Docker release bundles before loading.
- Made updater maintenance status writes atomic and restricted their permissions.
- Removed unintentional error-stack disclosure on certificate-management API errors; verbose diagnostics now require explicit debug opt-in.
- Added Referrer-Policy and cross-domain policy response headers.

## Release engineering
- Prevents reusing published release tags or overwriting release assets.
- Includes build provenance and SBOM attestations in registry publishing.
- Adds regression coverage for archive parsing, update lifecycle guards and publication policy.
- Includes a read-only deployment security audit tool and updated vulnerability disclosure instructions.

## Important limitations
- SHA-256 sums hosted alongside releases are integrity checks, **not independently signed publisher authentication**.
- SBOM generation does not in itself mean all dependencies are free of vulnerabilities.
- Existing deployments must still restrict management port 81 to trusted networks.
- Compatibility of customized OpenResty/Lua extensions must be validated when using standard NGINX.

## Upgrade and recovery
1. Back up persistent NPMi data and Let's Encrypt certificates.
2. Use Settings → Update when v1.7.0 is published; upgrades should preserve the existing installation and configuration.
3. Validate management API, proxy routing, TLS certificate renewals and NPMX peer health.
4. The Reinstall Current Release action reapplies the immutable released version. Software changes require a new release number.
5. For failures, use the existing rollback workflow and retain off-host backups.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/gigabytegrove/npm-improved/blob/develop/CHANGELOG.md
